Good questions

Feeds or personal calendars?

Feeds (Club, Moon, Sky, Essentials) are the same sky for everyone and keep updating while you subscribe. Personal calendars (Natal, Divination, Ritual, Convergence, Complete) are built from your birth chart and are a one-time purchase.

How does a calendar feed work?

After you buy, Gumroad gives you a subscribe link. Tap it on your phone or paste it into your calendar app once, and events appear on their own from then on.

Which calendar apps work?

Apple Calendar on iPhone, iPad and Mac, Google Calendar and Outlook. Anything that can subscribe to a calendar by link.

What do you need for a natal reading?

Your birth date, the exact time from your birth certificate if you have it, and the city you were born in.

What house system do you use?

Whole Sign houses, with Porphyry checked alongside, and traditional rulerships throughout.

Mercury and Venus retrograde, fall 2026: the dates and what to do

Two retrogrades, one Scorpio season, and both planets turn direct on the same day. Here is the whole timeline.

Transits · September 30, 2026 · 6 min read · by Patty

This fall we get a double feature. Venus stations retrograde in early October, Mercury follows three weeks later, and both of them turn direct on the same day in November. Most of it happens in Scorpio, which means the themes are not small talk: money you share with other people, trust, intimacy, secrets, and the stuff you would rather not look at.

Here are the dates, calculated with Swiss Ephemeris, and what to actually do with them.

The timeline

Aug 31Venus enters her pre-shadow
Oct 3Venus stations retrograde at 8°29′ Scorpio
Oct 4Mercury enters his pre-shadow
Oct 24Mercury stations retrograde at 20°59′ Scorpio
Oct 25Venus backs into Libra
Nov 13Mercury stations direct at 5°02′ Scorpio
Nov 13Venus stations direct at 22°52′ Libra
Nov 30Mercury leaves his post-shadow
Dec 15Venus leaves her post-shadow

Dates are for US Eastern time. A station can land on a different calendar day depending on where you live, so if you are cutting it close, check the exact time in your own time zone.

What the shadow is

A retrograde does not start on the station date. The planet first crosses the degree where it will later turn direct. That is the pre-shadow, and it is where the topic usually first shows up. After the planet turns direct it has to walk back over the same stretch of sky. That is the post-shadow, and it is where things get settled. If something weird starts in early October, that is not a coincidence. That is the preview.

Venus retrograde in Scorpio and Libra

Venus rules what we value and who we let close. Retrograde in Scorpio, she goes looking for the truth under a relationship: who holds the power, who owes what, what was never said out loud. Then she backs into Libra, her own sign, and the question shifts to fairness. Is this actually balanced, or have you been doing all the adjusting?

Exes come back during Venus retrogrades. That does not mean they should stay. Use this stretch to review, not to relaunch.

Mercury retrograde in Scorpio

Mercury in Scorpio is already a detective. Retrograde, he digs. Expect old information to resurface, conversations you thought were finished to reopen, and a strong urge to read between every line. The classic advice still stands: back up your files, reread contracts, and give messages an extra beat before you hit send.

What to actually do

  • Revisit, rewrite and renegotiate. The "re" words are the whole point.
  • Put the station dates in your calendar so they do not sneak up on you.
  • Look at which house of your chart Scorpio and Libra fall in. That is the part of your life this is about.
  • Save the big launches and signatures for after November 13 if you can, and after the post-shadow if you really want to be safe.

Every date in this post is already in the Cosmic Sky feed, shadows included, so it will show up in your phone calendar on its own.

What is a void-of-course Moon, and should you wait it out?

The short version: it is the Moon between jobs. Here is what that means and when it actually matters.

Moon · September 24, 2026 · 5 min read · by Patty

You have probably seen "Moon void of course" pop up in an astrology app and wondered if you are supposed to cancel your plans. Usually, no. But it is worth understanding, because some of the time it really does matter.

The definition

The Moon moves through a whole sign in about two and a half days. While it is in a sign, it makes aspects to the other planets: conjunctions, sextiles, squares, trines and oppositions. After it makes its last major aspect in that sign, and until it enters the next sign, it is void of course.

That window can be a few minutes or more than a day. The Moon is not broken during it. It is just not connecting to anything, so it is between jobs.

Why astrologers care

The traditional reading is that things started during a void Moon tend to come to nothing, or go somewhere you did not plan. The Moon is the part of an event that carries it forward, and a void Moon has nothing left to carry it to.

In practice, that looks like the meeting that goes nowhere, the order that gets lost, or the plan that quietly dissolves by next week.

When it actually matters

  • Starting something you want to grow: a launch, a signature, a first date you have high hopes for.
  • Elections, where you are picking a time to begin something on purpose.
  • Long void periods during a day that is already loaded, like a retrograde station or an eclipse.

When it does not

  • Routine tasks, errands, chores and anything already in motion.
  • Rest, meditation, cleaning, reading and finishing old projects. Void Moons are honestly great for these.
  • A short void of a few minutes. Do not build your life around those.

How to track it

You do not need to check an app every morning. Every void-of-course Moon is in the Cosmic Moon calendar feed, with the start and end time, so you can see it next to your plans and decide if it matters for what you are doing that day.

How to add astrology to your calendar (and forget about it)

Subscribe once and every Moon phase, retrograde and ingress shows up next to your plans. Here is how on iPhone, Mac and Google.

How to · September 18, 2026 · 4 min read · by Patty

Most astrology apps want you to open them every day. A calendar feed is the opposite: you set it up once, and the sky just shows up in the calendar you already use. Retrogrades next to your dentist appointment. The Full Moon next to your dinner plans.

What a calendar feed is

A feed is a link that ends in .ics. When you subscribe to it, your calendar app checks it for updates on its own. Nothing to download, nothing to reinstall when new events are added. If a date is corrected, your calendar picks it up.

iPhone and iPad

  1. Copy the feed link from your purchase.
  2. Open Settings, then Calendar, then Accounts.
  3. Tap Add Account, then Other, then Add Subscribed Calendar.
  4. Paste the link, tap Next, then Save.

On most links you can also just tap it on your phone and it will ask if you want to subscribe.

Mac

  1. Open Calendar.
  2. Choose File, then New Calendar Subscription.
  3. Paste the link and click Subscribe.
  4. Pick a color and how often it should refresh. Once a day is plenty.

Google Calendar

  1. Open Google Calendar on a computer.
  2. Next to Other calendars, click the plus sign, then From URL.
  3. Paste the link and click Add calendar.

Google refreshes subscribed calendars on its own schedule, so updates can take a while to show up. Apple Calendar is faster.

Keep it from getting noisy

  • Give each feed its own color so you can tell the Moon from the planets at a glance.
  • Turn a calendar off when you do not need it. It stays subscribed, just hidden.
  • Leave alerts off for the feed and turn them on for the few events you care about.

Cosmic Moon, Cosmic Sky, Essentials and the Club all work this way. Subscribe once and they keep themselves current.

Whole Sign vs Porphyry: why your planets moved houses

Same birth time, different app, different houses. You did not do anything wrong. You switched house systems.

Natal chart · September 10, 2026 · 5 min read · by Patty

You put your birth data into a new app and suddenly your Venus is in a different house. Nothing about your birth changed. The app is using a different house system, which is just a different way of dividing the sky into twelve parts.

Whole Sign houses

Whole Sign is the oldest system and the simplest. Whatever sign is rising becomes your entire 1st house, from 0° to 29°. The next sign is the 2nd house, and so on around the wheel. Every house is exactly one sign.

It is clean, it makes house rulers easy to follow, and it is what a lot of traditional and Hellenistic astrologers use.

Porphyry houses

Porphyry is a quadrant system. It starts with the four angles: the Ascendant, the IC, the Descendant and the Midheaven. Then it splits each of the four spaces between them into three equal houses.

Because the angles are not evenly spaced, the houses come out different sizes, and a house can start in the middle of a sign.

Why your planets move

A planet near the start or end of a sign is the one most likely to switch houses between systems. Say you have Libra rising at 25°. In Whole Sign, a planet at 5° Libra is in your 1st house. In Porphyry, the 1st house does not start until 25° Libra, so that same planet lands in your 12th.

Which one is right?

Neither is a mistake. They answer slightly different questions. Whole Sign is great for seeing which areas of life a sign and its ruler govern. Quadrant systems like Porphyry are more sensitive to the angles and how the sky was actually tilted when you were born.

My natal readings use Whole Sign, with Porphyry checked alongside. The personal calendars default to Porphyry, and you can ask for a different system when you order. If a planet changes houses between the two, that is worth reading both ways. It usually means the planet works in both areas of your life.
